framework: AP French Language and Culture Course and Exam Description (effective fall 2026)
subject: French Language and Culture

source.licence: © College Board; structure + our own wording only

topics.title: Skill Category 1: Interpretive Communication — Comprehend written texts, audio, and visualizations of data.

outcomes.text: Skill 1.A: Recognize explicit meaning.
Learning objective 1.A.1: Identify supporting or relevant details.
Learning objective 1.A.2: Identify data points, patterns, and trends.
Skill 1.B: Interpret meaning.
Learning objective 1.B.1: Determine the main idea, theme, or purpose.
Learning objective 1.B.2: Determine the intended audience.
Learning objective 1.B.3: Determine the point(s) of view, perspective(s), tone, or attitude.
Learning objective 1.B.4: Identify organizing and/or rhetorical structures and/or strategies.
Learning objective 1.B.5: Determine the meaning of words and phrases using textual cues.
Skill 1.C: Synthesize and infer meaning.
Learning objective 1.C.1: Connect information within or across sources.
Learning objective 1.C.2: Synthesize meaning to draw logical conclusions.
Learning objective 1.C.3: Infer implied meaning through context.

topics.title: Skill Category 2: Interpersonal and Presentational Communication — Speak and write in interpersonal and presentational contexts.

subtopics.title: Skill 2.A: Use language that aligns with the communicative purpose and context

outcomes.text: Skill 2.A: Use language that aligns with the communicative purpose and context.
Learning objective 2.A.1: Use a variety of grammatical structures.
Learning objective 2.A.2: Use a variety of vocabulary.
Learning objective 2.A.3: Use idiomatic and culturally relevant expressions.
Learning objective 2.A.4: Adopt an appropriate register for the intended audience and situation.

subtopics.title: Skill 2.B: Make communication comprehensible for the intended audience

outcomes.text: Skill 2.B: Make communication comprehensible for the intended audience.
Learning objective 2.B.1: Use communication strategies such as circumlocution and paraphrasing.
Learning objective 2.B.2: Monitor language production; recognize errors and attempt self-correction in spoken exchanges.
Learning objective 2.B.3: Use pronunciation that is comprehensible to a variety of speakers of the target language.
Learning objective 2.B.4: Use an appropriate rate of speech and effective intonation patterns.
Learning objective 2.B.5: Use standard conventions of written language (e.g., capitalization, orthography, accents, punctuation).

subtopics.title: Skill 2.C: Share ideas, information, and opinions about familiar and researched topics

outcomes.text: Skill 2.C: Share ideas, information, and opinions about familiar and researched topics.
Learning objective 2.C.1: Express ideas, preferences, and opinions.
Learning objective 2.C.2: Use research strategies to gather information and evidence.
Learning objective 2.C.3: Use examples to provide advice or information and to explain opinions or emotions.
Learning objective 2.C.4: Integrate information from multiple sources to develop and support a position or perspective.
Learning objective 2.C.5: Reference and cite sources appropriately.

subtopics.title: Skill 2.D: Apply organizational and rhetorical strategies

outcomes.text: Skill 2.D: Apply organizational and rhetorical strategies.
Learning objective 2.D.1: Apply an appropriate organizational structure.
Learning objective 2.D.2: Use a variety of cohesive devices (e.g., relative pronouns, pronoun referents, conjunctions, transitions) to effectively convey and connect ideas.

topics.title: Skill Category 3: Cultural Understanding — Demonstrate cultural understanding.

subtopics.title: Skill 3.A: Make connections within and across cultures

outcomes.text: Skill 3.A: Make connections within and across cultures.
Learning objective 3.A.1: Describe cultural products, practices, and perspectives.
Learning objective 3.A.2: Compare cultural products, practices, and perspectives among distinct communities.
Learning objective 3.A.3: Reflect on the significance of cultural products, practices, and perspectives.

topics.title: Essential questions and themes

outcomes.text: Explore the essential question: What constitutes a family in French-speaking societies? (Qu’est-ce qui constitue une famille dans les sociétés francophones ?)

Explore the essential question: What are some important aspects of family values and family life in French-speaking societies? (Quels sont quelques aspects importants des valeurs familiales et de la vie de famille dans les sociétés francophones ?)
Explore the essential question: How do families and communities experience today’s world? (Comment les familles et les communautés vivent-elles le monde d’aujourd’hui ?)
Explore how families shape values and traditions, as well as personal beliefs and interests.
Examine the experiences faced by families in modern society.
Consider the evolving role of the community in contemporary societies.

outcomes.text: Recommended instructional context: Community Activities (Les activités dans la communauté).
Recommended instructional context: Family Relationships (Les relations familiales).
Recommended instructional context: Social Interactions and Relationships (Les interactions et les relations sociales).
Recommended instructional context: Urban and Rural Communities (Les communautés urbaines et rurales).

Other recommended instructional contexts: Customs and Celebrations; Linguistics; French in the World; Education and Career; Food and Health; Pop Culture; Global Communication; History; Policy and Planning.

topics.title: Essential questions and themes

outcomes.text: Explore the essential question: How do language and culture influence each other? (Comment la langue et la culture s’influencent-elles mutuellement ?)
Explore the essential question: How do language and culture evolve over time? (En quoi langue et culture évoluent-elles au fil du temps ?)
Explore the essential question: How does technology influence language and culture? (Comment la technologie influence-t-elle la langue et la culture ?)
Explore how developments in science and technology impact language and the ways in which people communicate.
Examine how social media affects others.
Consider the role of entertainment and advertising as integral parts of culture.
Explore how a community’s values are reflected in its art and customs.

topics.title: Essential questions and themes

outcomes.text: Explore the essential question: How can art and creativity influence daily life? (Comment l’art et la créativité peuvent-ils influencer la vie quotidienne ?)
Explore the essential question: How does art both challenge and reflect cultural perspectives? (Comment l’art peut-il à la fois défier et refléter les perspectives culturelles ?)
Explore the essential question: How do communities value art and creativity? (Comment les communautés valorisent-elles l’art et la créativité ?)
Explore the essential question: How is art used to record history? (Comment l’art est-il utilisé pour raconter ou documenter l’histoire ?)
Explore how art and creativity influence the quality of life and values in a community.
Consider the role and importance of art in French-speaking communities.
Discover how the arts capture and reflect the history of a community.
Investigate how the concepts of art and creativity are defined within a culture.
Explore how art challenges and reflects cultural perspectives.
